newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia threatens "firm action" against parades.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia threatens "firm action" against parades.

text.p: Jakarta's military chief has warned of firm action against political party supporters if they continue to hold illegal street parades during Indonesia's election campaign, Media Indonesia newspaper reported on Monday.

The ultimatum came as the Moslem-orientated United Development Party (PPP), whose party faithful have frequently violated the ruling against street parades, prepared to resume campaigning across the capital on Monday afternoon.
The PPP cancelled campaigning on Friday after police placed restrictions on its planned gatherings.

"If they continue to commit violations, then we with great regret will have to take firm action," Jakarta military commander Major-General Sutiyoso was quoted as saying on Sunday by the privately run Media Indonesia newspaper.
Sutiyoso said the military were in a difficult and uncomfortable position because if they allowed the street parades to continue they would cause traffic jams and disturb public order.

The three legal parties, the PPP, the ruling Golkar and the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), are vying for the backing of nearly 125 million voters to fill 425 elected seats in the 500-seat House of Representatives. The other 75 seats are alloted to the military, which does not vote.
Campaigning for the May 29 poll began on April 27 and ends on May 23.

The ban on street parades was imposed for the first time during this campaign because of fears by authorities that they could spark violence after more than a dozen people were killed in political, religious and ethnic riots on the main island of Java in the past year.
The army said on Friday 29 people had died in traffic accidents during parades since the campaigning began.
The ban has been flouted by supporters from the three parties. Supporters ride on top of buses, trucks and motorcyles on some of Jakarta's key roads.

While police in several cities have written tickets for traffic violations, security forces have been mostly reduced to keeping the parades, sometimes involving tens of thousands of people, off the protocol roads in the capital.
"To prevent further victims, we do not have a choice but to act against (the parades)," Sutiyoso said.
"The party leaders must be responsible for the activities of their parties. Parades with open-backed vehicles or on motorcycles without helmets must be stopped," he added.

The Jakarta Post newspaper on Monday quoted Jakarta police as saying they had questioned 349 people for violations of election rules in the first eight days of campaign, including 238 cases of traffic violations by the three party contestants.

The official Antara news agency on Monday quoted Jakarta police chief Major-General Hamami Nata as saying police held 17 people for allegedly destroying PDI vehicles on Sunday. The report gave no further details of the incident.
Elsewhere on the weekend, a rally by the head of the PDI was disrupted in Jember in East Java by supporters of his ousted rival Megawati Sukarnoputri.
The Jakarta Post newspaper said 600 soldiers kept apart 200 Megawati supporters from 1,000 supporters of the government- backed PDI chief Surjadi. No clash was reported.

The paper also reported that thousands of PPP supporters in the South Sulawesi provincial capital of Ujung Pandang vandalised dozens of shop houses and a karoke bar during a fight with locals after a rally on Sunday.
One supporter of the ruling Golkar party was said to have been stabbed in the leg, but there were no reports of arrests.
